Adding technical notes ahead of the call — pulled from a quick gold-run against the same model and configuration:

Summary (short):
- Baseline p95 on our gold run: 96ms @ single-client steady state (8k prompt)
- At increased concurrency (40 simultaneous), p95 moves to ~150–180ms without batching refinement
- Turning on continuous prefix KV caching for repeated prompt headers cuts p95 by ~18% in our tests
- INT8 quantized build reduces per-token time but increases variance; recommend a canary on a small percentage first

Suggested quick tuning plan for the MAP checkpoint:
1) Kernel selection and pinned CPU affinities for the serving process — Marissa to prototype (ETA 4/25)
2) Batching policy: limit auto-batch window to 8ms for latency-sensitive routes — implement and test in pre-prod (owner: Marissa / Monica, ETA 05/03)
3) Enable prefix KV cache for top-10 repeated prompts (owner: Monica, ETA 04/28)
4) Quantized canary (INT8): run 5% traffic in dedicated pool; rollback policy: auto-fallback to float32 on p95 > 140ms (owner: Rishi, ETA 05/10)

I’ll prepare micro-bench scripts and a short runbook to reproduce these numbers — attaching the initial artifact in the MAP folder.

Marissa
Staff SWE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: rdw-map-weekly-tech-notes-20270418.txt (TXT)]

Looping back with the canary/playbook draft attached and a short note on the performance guardrails:

Key guardrails for INT8 canary (summary):
- Traffic slice: 5% isolated to dedicated pool
- p95 threshold (alert + immediate rollback): 140ms sustained over a 5-minute window
- Error-rate threshold: >1.5% request error rate triggers rollback
- Cost delta: expect ~12–18% cost reduction on the canary pool (monitor hourly)

Pre-prod run checklist (high level):
- KV cache enabled for repeated prompts (validate hit-rate > 55%)
- Batching policy set to 8ms window for target route
- Canary policy deployed with active telemetry and tracing
- Weekly MAP owner sign-off post run (Ben to confirm)

Attachments: rdw-canary-policy-v1.pdf, rdw-map-weekly-summary-20270422.pdf

I’ll stand by during the pre-prod window to monitor telemetry & automate rollback if thresholds hit. If we want, I can add an automatic fallback to the hosted float32 pool as an extra safety net.

Rishi
Principal, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
